text:
kevin: Quick check  traveling to Singapore next month. I've been told to book through company portal, but can I use my frequent-flyer miles for an upgrade and still get reimbursed for the ticket difference? Also, Singapore has some mandatory travel health forms for visitors is there any reimbursable cost for those?
people-ops: Short: you can use miles but the company reimburses only the cash component you paid. If using miles + cash upgrade, submit the portion you paid with card and note "FF miles used". Mandatory health forms (e.g., entry fees, mandatory tests) are reimbursable if required for business travel; attach proof.
kevin: If I use miles and pay taxes/fees on the ticket (e.g., fuel surcharge) does that get reimbursed?
finance-lina: Taxes and carrier-imposed fees paid in cash are reimbursable. Add a note about what part was paid vs covered by miles. If proof is only the carrier email, attach that.
security-ops: For Singapore business travels, ensure you register through the travel occupancy list and add emergency contact. Any health-related reimbursements need justification via consulate or official guidance.
kevin: Got it, thanks. Will book via portal, log the miles usage, and keep receipts for fees and forms.
people-ops: FYI: use the internal travel portal so travel insurance and company duty-of-care apply. Miles upgrades don't change insurance coverage for the same itinerary.
kevin: Awesome. I'll proceed. :thumbsup:
